jobs.title: Associate Director of Admission, Visits and Events at University of San Francisco
jobs.description: Employer: University of San Francisco Expires: 11/18/2026 Associate Director of Admission, Visits and Events University of San Francisco R0011849 USF Hilltop Campus Job Title:Associate Director of Admission, Visits and Events Job Summary:The Associate Director of Admission, Visits and Events provides strategic leadership in recruitment, admission, and enrollment services to support the University of San Francisco's undergraduate enrollment goals. As a member of the Office of Undergraduate Admission leadership team, the Associate develops and implements data-informed, mission-driven strategies to attract and engage prospective students throughout the admission lifecycle. A key function of this position is providing leadership and strategic oversight for the Welcome Center, the hub of the student visit experience for admissions, and for on-campus admission events. The Associate Director ensures these functions deliver an exceptional, student-centered experience that reflects the values and distinctiveness of a USF education. This position supervises professional staff, including the Welcome Center Manager (who manages the daily operations of the Welcome Center and student ambassador team) and the Events Manager (who leads signature admission events and yield programming). Through these teams, the Associate Director oversees the campus experience within Undergraduate Admission, fostering a unified and purpose-driven approach centering prospective students' engagement on campus. Reporting to the Director of Admission for Transfer and Campus Engagement, this position collaborates closely with SEM leadership and campus partners to ensure recruitment, outreach, and visit strategies align with the lived student experience at USF. This position must have experience in and enthusiasm for data reporting, analysis, and communications/marketing. Full Job Description: Job Description • In collaboration with the Director of Admission for Transfer and Campus Engagement, provide strategic leadership and direction for the Welcome Center, the campus visit experience and undergraduate admission events to communicate the value and distinctive qualities of a USF education. • Supervise, mentor, and support professional staff responsible for visit programs, student ambassador management, and on-campus events. • Develop and implement a comprehensive vision to increase student visit volume and enhance the visitor experience in collaboration with Enrollment Marketing. • Ensure a seamless and high-quality experience for all visitors, prospective students, and families through both on-campus and virtual programming. • Develop strong relationships with the high school and community college counseling community, admission volunteers, faculty, administrators, and SEM colleagues. • Use data and market analysis to inform strategies for developing, implementing, and continually assessing the strengths and opportunities for the visit program, and on-campus and virtual events. • Evaluate undergraduate applicants (first-year and transfer) and make admission decisions. • Establishes and maintains admission standards, requirements, protocols, policies, and procedures for enrollment, in collaboration with SEM leadership and schools and colleges. • Contribute to the development of marketing and communication strategies that support recruitment, visit programs, and events. • Selects, schedules, and coordinates high school and college fair visits to recruit prospective students. • Counsels prospective students and families about admission, financial aid, academic programs and student life at USF, explains tuition and fees, application and registration procedures, and career and corresponding educational planning. • Conducts information meetings and represents USF at education fairs, and other public events, with targeted outreach to traditional first-year and transfer students. Develops knowledge of competitor institutions in the region. • Develops and maintains effective relationships with counseling, teaching and administrative contacts at high schools and other institutions of higher education. • Works with the Director of Admission for Transfer and Campus Engagement in maintenance of the recruitment, visit and events budgets. • Performs other duties as assigned. Position Qualifications and Requirements: • Bachelor's degree; advanced degree preferred • 5-7 years of demonstrated experience in undergraduate admission • Demonstrated experience with campus visit programs, student ambassador or tour guide programs, and/or event or welcome center management. • Strategic thinker with proven ability to lead and motivate teams, manage complex projects, and build cross-campus relationships. • Acts responsibly toward, anticipates and addresses the needs of community partners and stakeholders. Strong focus on customer benefit and relationship building. Understands the industry and competitive landscape and recognizes the implications for the organization. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to present information in various formats to effectively communicate cross-generationally with a variety of persons and audiences. • Ability to work with minimal supervision, establish priorities, handle multiple tasks simultaneously, and follow through and meet deadlines. • Ability to think innovatively, creatively, strategically and collaboratively; effectively manages programs and facilitates thoughtful and insightful problem resolution. • Ability to multitask, work independently and as part of a team, establishing, building and retaining cooperative and collaborative working relationships while performing responsibilities. • Demonstrated analytical ability to use data for planning, assessment, and improvement. • Experience with CRM systems (Slate preferred) and reporting tools. • Ability to travel (estimated 25-30% of time) to various locations to build/maintain partnerships, attend events, and activities related to the responsibilities of the position. • Availability to work nights and weekends as needed. • Valid driver's license. • Commitment to Jesuit Catholic education, and the university's Mission, Vision, and Values. Full-Time/Part-Time:Full time Pay Rate:Salary Salary Range :$90,000 - 95,000 annualized; commensurate with experience To apply, visit https://apptrkr.com/6730079. The University of San Francisco is located in the heart of one of the world’s most innovative and diverse cities, and is home to a vibrant academic community of students and faculty who achieve excellence in their fields. Its diverse student body enjoys direct access to faculty, small classes and outstanding opportunities in the city itself. USF is San Francisco's first university, and its Jesuit Catholic mission helps ignite a student’s passion for social justice and a desire to “Change the World From Here.” For more information, visit http://www.usfca.edu. jobs.description: Employer: Virginia Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services Expires: 11/18/2026 Hiring Range: Anticipated starting salary: $47,340–$50,917, commensurate with experienceAbout the AgencyVDDHH is a small Department with a dynamic team of dedicated and passionate deaf and hearing professionals working in a fast-paced environment. VDDHH statewide services are organized into 3 niche industries in telecommunications, interpreting and community services. We strive for continuous improvements seeking to streamline operations for maximum efficiency and effectiveness.About the PositionThe Virginia Department for the Deaf & Hard of Hearing is seeking an Interpreter Services Coordinator to coordinate the VDDHH Interpreter Services Program. This position provides direct customer service and program support to the Interpreter Services Program by coordinating requested interpreter services for Virginia State Agencies, the Supreme Court of Virginia, the Virginia Court System, and other organizations throughout the Commonwealth of Virginia as appropriate.This position also provides programmatic information to consumers, creates informational material, processes payment vouchers/invoices for interpreter services, performs related data processing, and maintains accurate and appropriate records of such transactions. This position is also responsible for ensuring all interpreters whose services are coordinated are appropriately qualified and registered with VDDHH and eVA.Joh Duties and ResponsibilitiesCoordination and Referral of Interpreter ServicesSummary:Coordinates and schedules qualified interpreters and CART providers for state agencies and courts.Key Tasks:• Coordinate and refer interpreters/CART services promptly.• Provide guidance on effective communication and interpreter use.• Maintain accurate Interpreter Request Forms and update changes within one day.• Ensure all required information is complete for efficient service delivery.• Contact qualified contract interpreters to secure coverage.• Communicate with state agencies, courts, and public contacts professionally.Records Maintenance / Materials ManagementSummary:Organizes and maintains interpreter records and program data.Key Tasks:• Maintain spreadsheets and tools for statistical tracking.• Update the Directory of Qualified Interpreters.• Organize ISP files and archive materials.• Prepare annual vendor mailings.• Maintain and distribute listings for emergency response and specialty interpreters.Technical Assistance and Program SupportSummary:Provides information, support, and guidance on ISP procedures to interpreters, agencies, and courts.Key Tasks:• Provide orientation and assistance on interpreting procedures, billing, and payment.• Develop presentations and informational materials.• Support agency projects and initiatives.• Coordinate with VQAS staff to maintain accurate level information.• Respond promptly and professionally to inquiries.• Research interpreting-related topics and support special projects.• Assist with administrative tasks and emergency response as needed.Invoice ProcessingSummary:Verifies and processes interpreter and CART invoices.Key Tasks:• Review invoices for accuracy against request forms.• Research and correct discrepancies.• Prepare vouchers and submit payments per policy.• Total monthly interpreter/CART expenditures.Minimum Qualifications• Considerable knowledge of deaf culture and the communication requirements of persons who are deaf and hard of hearing, specifically in the area of interpreting needs and services.• Demonstrated ability in accurate data entry, data management, and detail-oriented tasks.• Demonstrated ability to work independently in support of Agency and Program priorities, work scheduled days / hours, and work in a team environment• Understand and appropriately apply established policies and procedures to individual situations; in unique or special situations, research and recommend / implement appropriate problem resolution, and adapt to change• Demonstrated effective written, verbal, and sign language communication skills with a diverse customer base.Education, Experience, Licensure, Certification Required for Entry into Position:Professional experience delivering programs for deaf, hard of hearing and/or deafblind individuals.Professional experience providing administrative support.American Sign Language Proficiency Interview (ASLPI) evaluation at Level 2+ or equivalent is required for the positionAdditional ConsiderationsN/ASpecial InstructionsBenefits:Deaf & Hard of Hearing offers a comprehensive benefits package to include your choice of health insurance plans, flexible spending accounts, VRS retirement, employer paid basic group life insurance, employee paid optional group life, 13 paid holidays, Sick Leave, Annual Leave, Family Personal Leave, employee discount programs, and much more!

jobs.description: Employer: Kern Community College District Expires: 11/18/2026 Child Development Center Associate Teacher (11 months/year)Kern Community College District Salary: $37,335.36 - $51,926.64 Annually33.0Job Type: ClassifiedJob Number: FY25-2600389Location: Bakersfield College -- Panorama Campus, CADepartment: Child Development Center Below is our job description for this position. Please also review the Important Instructions & Additional Information section below, which contains valuable information about our application process.Basic FunctionUnder supervision, provide assistance to the classroom teacher in the care, development, and instruction of preschool children and infants in a child development center program.Representative DutiesAssist the Teacher in planning and coordination of classroom activities and instruction; develop and maintain developmentally appropriate, safe learning environments.Supervise and directly interact with children in a warm and positive manner.Prepare age and developmentally appropriate lesson outlines, plans, and other activities for science, math, music, art, language, social, emotional, and physical development of the children; submit to Teacher for review.Conduct demonstrations and learning activities for children.Serve as primary caregiver for an assigned group of children; perform initial and periodic state required evaluations.Conduct conferences with parents to discuss child status, progress, and problems; assist in developing and implementing conflict management and problem solving strategies with children.Follow center policies and procedures including those for health and safety; provide information to employees, volunteers, students, and families on health, safety, and transportation, and other policies.Oversee groups of children in various indoor and outdoor activities; set up and disassemble playground equipment; assure safe indoor and outdoor play.Supervise the use of the restrooms; change and launder wet or soiled clothes; change diapers; assist in toilet training.Prepare and serve nutritional snacks and lunches; prepare bottles, formulas and infant meals; assist in preparing and revising basic menus; supervise snack and meal times.Administer basic First Aid as needed; teach and encourage good health and safety habits.Perform light housekeeping duties including washing dishes, clearing lunch tables, sweeping floors, and emptying waste receptacles; maintain the classroom and outdoor environment in a safe, sanitary, and orderly condition.Operate a variety of classroom equipment and appliances including a copier, laminator, paper cutter, computer, vacuum cleaner, washer, dryer, and microwave; assure proper food storage; sterilize kitchen area; maintain food production worksheets.Maintain appropriate records as requested.Assist in identifying special needs of children and/or families.Oversee and participate in evaluation of laboratory students and the supervision of activities.Perform related duties as assigned.Minimum QualificationsAny combination equivalent to: graduation from high school supplemented by twelve semester units of course work in early childhood education or a related field and one year of experience working with children in an organized setting. Possession of, or eligibility to obtain and retain, a Child Development Associate Teacher Permit issued by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing.LICENSES AND OTHER REQUIREMENTSMaintain satisfactory level of progress toward and the successful completion of the Professional Development requirement for Permit renewal.Completion of pediatric CPR and first aid training through an accredited or approved program.Possession of a current pediatric CPR and first aid certificate.Satisfactory completion of a pre-employment physical assessment.Satisfactory completion of pre-employment drug testing.Clear criminal record check including fingerprints.Knowledge & AbilitiesKNOWLEDGE OFEarly childhood education programs, practices, and techniques.Current best practices for inclusive early childhood education.Instructional and tutorial techniques.Requirements of maintaining a children's center in a safe, clean, and orderly condition.Policies and objectives of assigned program and activities.Interpersonal skills using tact, patience, and courtesy.Health and safety regulations.Principles and practices of personal hygiene.Sanitation practices related to handling and serving food.Basic First Aid techniques.ABILITY TODevelop age and developmentally appropriate lesson plans and outlines.Effectively conduct activities for children.Monitor the behavior of young children and oversee activities.Maintain a children's center in a safe, clean, and orderly condition.Apply basic principles and practices of nutrition.Administer basic First Aid. Understand and follow oral and written directions.Prepare and serve food in accordance with health and safety regulations.Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others.Observe health and safety regulations. jobs.title: Venture School Instructor at Venture Upward
jobs.description: Employer: Venture Upward Expires: 11/18/2026 Title: Venture School Instructor Venture School is Venture Upward’s weekly, in-person enrichment day, and for many students, it is the highlight of their week. Venture School Instructors are not babysitters, activity leaders, or club coordinators. They are Learning Architects who design hands-on, academically enriching classes that students cannot wait to return to. Every class is built to do two things at once: make every child feel seen and inspired while giving families confidence that their child’s time is safe, meaningful, and genuinely worth it. If you love making learning exciting, believe relationships come before curriculum, and notice the quiet child in the back of the room, you will thrive here.Venture School operates one day each week for approximately 4.5 hours and is led by a Site Manager who supports a team of instructors and assistants. A typical school day includes four enrichment classes and a lunch period, with classes lasting 45 to 60 minutes. Locations typically serve 20–100 students, with average class sizes of about 15 students. Each classroom is led by one instructor and supported by either a classroom assistant or a floating assistant, as needed. While Venture School classes are academically enriching and intentionally designed to spark curiosity, they complement home education rather than replace it and generally do not include homework or formal assessments.Design and teach hands-on classes that advance a meaningful academic discipline. At Venture School, we do not simply build with Legos. We explore architecture. We do not just cook. We discover the chemistry behind every recipe. Plan each class around the Venture Lesson structure, so students connect with why a topic matters, discover meaningful content, create something of their own, reflect on what they learned, and leave inspired to learn more. Arrive prepared, organized, and on time each week. Build at least one memorable moment of wonder into every class, the kind of “whoa” moment students talk about at home. Know every student by name, along with their interests, strengths, and challenges, so each child feels seen and valued. You do not need to be a licensed teacher for this position. Requirements:*Good time management*Love of learning and excitement to pass that on* Able to come up with a class plan or follow one provided for you that helps engage children in a fun and educational way. *Be able to pass a background check

Ensure that students with disabilities are receiving a free appropriate education in the least restrictive environment (LRE). 18. jobs.title: Academic Coach at College Living Experience
jobs.description: Employer: College Living Experience Expires: 11/19/2026 Young Adult Transition ProgramJob Type: Part-timeHours: Approximately 15 hours per weekWork Location: In person – Austin, TXStart Date: ASAPPay: $18-$20 per hour Are you looking for a job where your work truly matters, every day is different, and you get to be part of a fun and supportive community? At College Living Experience (CLE), academic success isn't built through grades alone. It happens during study sessions, conversations with professors, time-management planning, problem-solving challenges, and the everyday moments where students learn how to navigate college with greater confidence and independence. As an Academic Coach, you'll help neurodiverse young adults discover how they learn best and develop the skills needed to succeed in college and beyond. You'll work alongside students to strengthen executive functioning, organization, study habits, self-advocacy, and academic confidence while helping them navigate the challenges of higher education. We are looking for someone who is patient, creative, and passionate about helping students reach their potential. Someone who enjoys mentoring, adapting their approach to different learning styles, and celebrating growth along the way. Candidates often come from backgrounds in education, tutoring, special education, academic coaching, psychology, student support services, learning assistance, or humanities instruction. We especially welcome candidates with experience teaching or tutoring writing, English, literature, history, communications, philosophy, political science, or related fields. In this role, you'll provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring, help students develop effective study strategies, manage assignments and deadlines, communicate with professors, prepare for exams, and build the skills needed to become more independent learners. You'll collaborate closely with our social, career, and independent living teams to ensure students receive holistic support across all areas of their development.The ideal candidate believes that success looks different for every student and is excited to help neurodiverse young adults build confidence, overcome challenges, achieve their educational goals, and create a strong foundation for lifelong learning and independence. Why People Love Working at CLE Working at CLE means being part of a collaborative team dedicated to helping students achieve meaningful academic and personal growth. Every day is different. You'll work one-on-one with students, helping them navigate college coursework, develop effective learning strategies, and overcome challenges that may be impacting their success. You get to see real progress. One of the most rewarding aspects of this role is watching students gain confidence, improve their academic skills, and become more independent learners. You can be creative in your approach. No two students learn the same way. You'll have the flexibility to adapt strategies, develop individualized supports, and find innovative ways to help students succeed. You build meaningful relationships. Academic coaching at CLE goes beyond tutoring. You'll serve as a mentor, guide, and advocate as students navigate their college experience. You're part of a supportive team. Our academic, career, social, and independent living staff work closely together to provide holistic support and celebrate student successes. Academic Coaching & Executive Functioning Support Provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring based on each student's learning style, strengths, and academic goals. Review syllabi, assignments, grades, and course requirements to help students create realistic semester and weekly plans. Teach and reinforce executive functioning skills, including organization, time management, prioritization, task initiation, and study strategies. Help students prepare for exams, complete projects, and develop effective note-taking and learning techniques. Support students in communicating with professors, academic advisors, and campus Disability Support Services (DSS) when appropriate. Foster self-advocacy, problem-solving, and independent learning skills. Student Support & Collaboration Build strong mentoring relationships that encourage accountability, confidence, and personal growth. Collaborate with social, career development, and independent living staff to ensure students receive coordinated support across all domains. Participate in team meetings, student reviews, and problem-solving discussions. Documentation & Communication Document student progress, coaching sessions, and action plans in BestNotes following each student meeting. Communicate concerns, successes, and recommendations to the Academic Coordinator and interdisciplinary team. Maintain accurate records and support student goal tracking throughout the semester. BenefitsCLE offers a supportive work environment and benefits for eligible employees, which may include:• Dental insurance• Vision insurance• Retirement plan• Paid sick time• Flexible scheduling optionsRequirements Transportation RequirementsThis role includes travel between work sites and transporting students as needed.Applicants must:• Possess a valid driver’s license• Have at least one year of licensed driving experience• Meet company motor vehicle insurance requirements Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in psychology, education, social work, counseling, or a related field Teaching/tutoring experience (1+ year preferred). Experience supporting students with learning differences or special education (preferred). Strong communication skills and the ability to tailor instruction to individual learning needs. Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment

You get to see real progress. One of the most rewarding aspects of this role is watching students gain confidence, improve their academic skills, and become more independent learners. You can be creative in your approach. No two students learn the same way. You'll have the flexibility to adapt strategies, develop individualized supports, and find innovative ways to help students succeed. You build meaningful relationships. Academic coaching at CLE goes beyond tutoring. You'll serve as a mentor, guide, and advocate as students navigate their college experience. You're part of a supportive team. Our academic, career, social, and independent living staff work closely together to provide holistic support and celebrate student successes. Academic Coaching & Executive Functioning Support Provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring based on each student's learning style, strengths, and academic goals. Review syllabi, assignments, grades, and course requirements to help students create realistic semester and weekly plans. Teach and reinforce executive functioning skills, including organization, time management, prioritization, task initiation, and study strategies. Help students prepare for exams, complete projects, and develop effective note-taking and learning techniques. Support students in communicating with professors, academic advisors, and campus Disability Support Services (DSS) when appropriate. Foster self-advocacy, problem-solving, and independent learning skills. Student Support & Collaboration Build strong mentoring relationships that encourage accountability, confidence, and personal growth. Collaborate with social, career development, and independent living staff to ensure students receive coordinated support across all domains. Participate in team meetings, student reviews, and problem-solving discussions. Documentation & Communication Document student progress, coaching sessions, and action plans in BestNotes following each student meeting. Communicate concerns, successes, and recommendations to the Academic Coordinator and interdisciplinary team. Maintain accurate records and support student goal tracking throughout the semester. Experience supporting students with learning differences or special education (preferred). Strong communication skills and the ability to tailor instruction to individual learning needs. Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment

jobs.title: Afterschool Group Leader at Immigrant Social Services
jobs.description: Employer: Immigrant Social Services Expires: 11/19/2026 2026–2027 Afterschool Programs Group LeaderPosition SummaryImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is seeking enthusiastic, dependable, and compassionate individuals who are passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of children and families. Group Leaders play an important role in creating safe, engaging, and inclusive afterschool environments where students can learn, build confidence, develop meaningful relationships, and discover their strengths.Serving students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Group Leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment activities, recreation, and evidence-based social-emotional learning experiences that promote academic success and healthy youth development. Every interaction—from helping a student solve a challenging homework problem to leading a cooperative game or supporting a child through a difficult moment—is an opportunity to foster resilience, confidence, and lifelong skills.Group Leaders receive comprehensive training and ongoing coaching to facilitate evidence-based curricula that strengthen students' social-emotional competencies, build protective factors, and promote healthy decision-making. Group Leaders are more than activity leaders—they are mentors, educators, and trusted adults who help children develop the skills they need to thrive both in and beyond the classroom.About ISS Afterschool ProgramsServing students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Immigrant Social Services (ISS) operates afterschool programs at public school sites throughout Manhattan’s Lower East Side and Chinatown. We see the out-of-school time space as an opportunity to reimagine learning, achievement, and youth development in ways that respond to the lived realities, strengths, and aspirations of immigrant students and their families.Social-emotional learning (SEL) forms the core of our afterschool programs. Through evidence-based SEL experiences, students develop the skills and mindsets they need to navigate relationships, manage emotions, solve problems, make responsible decisions, and build confidence and resilience. Whether helping a student work through a challenging homework problem, facilitating a cooperative game, or supporting a child through a difficult moment, every interaction is an opportunity to strengthen social-emotional skills and promote healthy development.Our work is grounded in Positive Youth Development (PYD), which recognizes young people as capable, resourceful individuals with strengths, ideas, and contributions to make. We create environments where students can build meaningful relationships with adults and peers, develop a sense of belonging, exercise agency, explore their interests, and experience success. Rather than focusing only on what young people need to overcome, our programs intentionally cultivate the protective factors, relationships, and opportunities that help children thrive.Within this SEL and Positive Youth Development framework, group leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment, recreation, and hands-on learning experiences that promote academic success and whole-child development. Program activities and curricular content integrate language arts and literacy, STEM, social studies, the arts, health and fitness, and social and emotional development—while creating space for curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, and compassion.Core ResponsibilitiesCreate Safe, Inclusive, and Supportive Learning EnvironmentsGroup Leaders help create spaces where every child feels physically and emotionally safe, welcomed, and valued.Responsibilities include:Supervise students and ensure their safety and wellbeing throughout all afterschool activities.Foster a welcoming, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed environment where children feel respected, included, and encouraged to participate.Build caring, supportive relationships that promote trust, belonging, and positive youth development.Encourage cooperation, responsibility, and respect through positive behavior support,and developmentally appropriate classroom management.Model professionalism, empathy, patience, and positive communication in all interactions with students, families, school staff, and colleagues.Recognize and respond appropriately to students' individual developmental, social emotional, and behavioral needs.Support Students Throughout the Afterschool ExperienceEvery afternoon is different. Group Leaders help create a smooth, engaging, and supportive afterschool experience by confidently guiding groups of students through a variety of activities, settings, and learning experiences. Success in this role requires flexibility, sound judgment, and the ability to adapt to students' changing needs throughout the day.Group Leaders are responsible for:Guiding students through the many parts of the afterschool day, including arrival, snack, homework, enrichment, recreation, and dismissal.Supervising students in a variety of settings, including classrooms, cafeterias, gymnasiums, playgrounds, hallways, and other shared spaces.Leading safe, organized, and positive transitions between activities while maintaining student engagement and appropriate behavior.Providing academic support and facilitating homework support in both small- and large-group settings.Recognizing when students need additional encouragement, redirection, or emotional support and responding with patience, empathy, and professionalism.Creating opportunities throughout the afternoon for students to practice leadership, cooperation, communication, and responsible decision-making.Facilitate Social-Emotional Learning ISS believes children develop important life skills through meaningful relationships, engaging learning experiences, and opportunities to practice positive behaviors every day. Group Leaders play an active role in helping students build the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to succeed in school and life.After completing ISS training and receiving ongoing coaching, Group Leaders facilitate evidence-based Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curricula while reinforcing these skills throughout daily interactions, activities, and routines.Group Leaders help students develop:Self-awareness and self-confidenceSelf-management and emotional regulationResponsible decision-makingPositive relationship skillsSocial awareness and empathyCommunication and conflict resolution skillsProblem-solving and critical thinkingLeadership, teamwork, and cooperationBy integrating these skills into homework support, enrichment activities, recreation, and everyday interactions, Group Leaders help children build habits that contribute to long-term academic success and healthy development.Collaboration & Professional ResponsibilitiesHigh-quality afterschool programs are built through teamwork, communication, and a shared commitment to helping children succeed. Group Leaders work closely with Site Directors, fellow staff, school personnel, and families to provide a consistent, supportive experience for every student.Responsibilities include:Collaborate with Site Directors, school staff, and fellow Group Leaders to provide engaging, high-quality programming.Communicate professionally with colleagues, families, and school personnel to support student success and well-being.Promptly report concerns related to student safety, attendance, behavior, or well-being to supervisory staff.Participate actively in staff meetings, trainings, coaching sessions, and professional development opportunities.Maintain accurate attendance, lesson implementation records, and other required program documentation.Carry out responsibilities in accordance with ISS's mission, positive youth development philosophy, and organizational values.QualificationsWe're looking for individuals who enjoy working with children, are eager to learn, and are excited to make a positive impact in their community.Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled in college or have completed some college coursework.At least 18 years of age.Experience working with children in schools, afterschool programs, camps, tutoring programs, childcare settings, or other youth-serving organizations.Experience leading activities or facilitating groups of children.Ability to work during afterschool hours throughout the school year.Strong communication and interpersonal skills.Dependable, professional, and committed to creating a positive experience for children.Preferred QualificationsAbility to build supportive relationships with children and families from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds.Effective classroom management and positive behavior support skills.Strong situational judgment and adaptability, with the ability to recognize what each moment calls for—whether supporting an individual student, guiding a small group, managing transitions, or leading engaging activities for a larger group.Comfortable working in an active, fast-paced environment where schedules, settings, and student needs change throughout the afternoon.Willingness to receive coaching and implement evidence-based curricula with fidelity.Commitment to continuous professional growth and reflective practice.Bilingual in Mandarin, Cantonese, Fujianese, or Spanish preferred.Experience working with immigrant, multilingual, and underserved communities is highly desirable.Why Join ISS?At ISS, you'll do more than supervise children after school—you'll become part of a mission-driven organization dedicated to strengthening immigrant communities through education, prevention, and youth development.As an ISS Group Leader, you'll gain valuable professional experience while making a lasting impact on the lives of children and families. Whether you're pursuing a career in education, psychology, counseling, social work, public health, or another care profession, this position provides meaningful opportunities to develop practical skills that will support your future career.What You'll GainHands-on experience working with elementary-aged children in a school-based setting.Paid training in evidence-based Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curricula.Coaching from experienced youth development professionals.Experience facilitating engaging lessons, enrichment activities, and group discussions.Leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills that transfer across education and human services careers.Experience working with culturally and linguistically diverse children and families.Opportunities to build your resume while making a meaningful difference in your community.At ISS, we believe investing in our staff is essential to providing high-quality programs for children. We are committed to supporting your growth as a youth development professional through training, mentorship, and continuous learning.Hours and Commitment: This is a part-time/contract position for the 2026-27 school year that follows the NYC DOE academic calendar. Must be available during afterschool hours, Monday–Friday, 2:00 pm/2:30 pm – 5:45 pm/6:00 pm (start and end times depend on location). Flexible days, but five days a week is preferred. Hiring is contingent upon passing a background check. Location: Our afterschool programs operate at public school sites in the Lower East Side/Chinatown neighborhood.Payrate: $17.00 - $18.00 per hour - depending on experienceApplication Process:To apply, please email your resume and cover letter to hr@issnyc.org with the subject line: Afterschool Programs Group Leader. About ISSFounded in 1972, Immigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the conditions of underserved immigrants in Chinatown/Lower East Side, New York City. The majority of immigrant families we serve are from low-income, monolingual Chinese-speaking multigenerational households. Through programs and services centered on care, education, prevention, and community, we nurture and empower immigrant children/youth, young adults, seniors, and families to develop and restore their agency to strengthen the wellbeing of their communities. For more information, visit www.issnyc.org. Equal Opportunity EmploymentImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.title: High School Special Education Teacher at Environmental Charter School
jobs.description: Employer: Environmental Charter School Expires: 11/19/2026 The Environmental Charter School is seeking a highly dedicated and motivated Special Education Teacher for our upcoming school year (2026-27). Successful candidates must be progressive-minded and embody a can-do spirit and work ethic. For best consideration, candidates should have a degree or experience in education, a strong work ethic, and a “whatever it takes” attitude.OUR PHILOSOPHY AND MISSIONAs the world changes and becomes increasingly more complex, global citizens will need to be equipped with skills to be flexible thinkers, creative problem solvers, and effective leaders. ECS offers a program that develops students into critical thinkers, thoughtful innovators, and well-rounded scholars. We provide students with the tools and educational foundation to become tomorrow’s global citizens, and we strive to teach students how their choices impact the world around them. By using environmental content as a lens for instruction, ECS provides students with a context in which to explore ideas and observations, to practice inquiry, and to actively problem-solve. Throughout their academic career at ECS, students build core skills across all disciplines and then actively apply these skills to support the impact of learning.WORKING AT THE ENVIRONMENTAL CHARTER SCHOOLThe Environmental Charter School’s faculty and staff are passionate, talented, and uncompromising with a mission to make sure all students succeed at a high level. Every aspect of our organization and program is designed and continually refined to ensure that goal. Our work is student-centered, constantly improving, and reflective. ECS’s progressive approach to education challenges faculty to take risks. We strongly value collaboration and recognize the power of systems thinking. Our high achievement scores, long waiting list (nearly 200 students in kindergarten alone!), and unique location in the city of Pittsburgh serve as a model in environmentally focused education.OVERVIEWThe ECS Special Education Teacher is an intervention, differentiation, and curriculum adaptation specialist. Working collaboratively with general education teachers, education assistants, paraprofessionals, building specialists, and the Campus Leadership Team, the ECS special education teacher provides the modifications and adaptations that students need to participate in rigorous and engaging learning opportunities in the classroom. Special education teachers work to ensure all students (K-5) are supported through case management across or within grade levels as determined by the Campus Leadership Team. Candidates should be energetic and progressive-minded, with a willingness to work collaboratively with the building staff.KEY RESPONSIBILITIESWorks with the general education teachers to modify and adapt curriculum and PBL experiences for students with disabilities based upon a variety of instructional techniquesCollaborates with parents, administrators, school psychologists, and other professionals to develop individualized education programs (IEPs) designed to promote students’ educational, physical, and social/emotional development Provides instruction or instructional supports in all academic subjects using a variety of techniques to reinforce learning and to meet students’ varying needs and interestsProvides direct and indirect instructional support to students in a variety of settings, including small group, one-on-one, and inclusive classroom settingsFacilitate a positive, achievement-oriented, and structured learning environment in which all students can experience success Implement school-wide behavior management policies and the Olweus Bullying Prevention program within classrooms and throughout the schoolMaintain accurate and complete student records and prepare reports required by laws, district policies, and administrative regulations in a timely and professional manner Collect and maintain data to track student progress, drive individualized instruction, and to design academic interventionsMaintain professional competence by participating in opportunities for professional growthServe as the case manager for students with IEPs and communicate regularly with families to share academic and behavioral progress and develop a supportive home-school relationship Educational Background and Work ExperienceBachelor’s degree from an accredited institution PA Certification in special education; dual certification in Math or ELA preferredAt least 3 years of teaching experience preferredFamiliarity with charter schools and high school students desirableCompensation and BenefitsMinimum starting salary of $44,716 plus a $1000 special education supplement. Additional compensation may be awarded to highly qualified individuals.Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance, generous paid time off, and participation in a generous 403b retirement plan, and voluntary coverage optionsTo ApplyPlease submit a cover letter, resume, and a copy of your current PA certification to: https://ecspgh.org/careers/.Clearances current within one year of hire date will be required and include Arrest & Conviction Disclosure, Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance (Act 151), Pennsylvania State Police Criminal Record Clearance (Act 34), and FBI Criminal Background Check (Act 114). Commonwealth of PA Sexual Misconduct/Abuse Disclosure. Release (Act 168) will also be required.ECS is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Lead Teacher/Montessori Guide Preschool at Bishop Baraga Academy
jobs.description: Employer: Bishop Baraga Academy Expires: 11/19/2026 Lead Teacher/Montessori Guide Preschool## What if working in childcare felt different?You love working with children. But that doesn’t mean you have to love **chaos, unpredictable schedules, working weekends, or feeling burned out.**At **Bishop Baraga Academy**, we’ve intentionally built a different kind of childcare and preschool workplace.🌿 **Montessori changes your day.** Our thoughtfully prepared classrooms encourage children to become increasingly independent—which means less entertaining and managing and more **guiding, observing, teaching, and building relationships.**### You might be a great fit for BBA if you are:- **Punctual and dependable** — people can count on you.- **Energetic and positive** — you genuinely enjoy engaging with young children.- **Excited to teach** — you enjoy modeling behaviors and introducing new ideas.- **Kind and patient** — you use a calm, respectful teaching voice, even during difficult moments.- **A positive role model** — you know children are always learning from the adults around them.- **Ready to grow** — you welcome coaching, feedback, professional development, and courses.- **Focused on independence** — you enjoy teaching children to do things for themselves.**Montessori experience? Great! No Montessori experience? We can teach you.**### And here's what you can expect from us:🎓 **You are an educator—not a babysitter.** You will be treated like a professional teacher and Montessori Guide doing meaningful work that goes far beyond supervising play.🤝 **A team you will want to work with.** Supportive teammates, strong leadership, and a tight-knit community of families.📋 **A professionally operated workplace.** We aren't family-run. BBA operates with established policies, procedures, leadership, expectations, and employee benefits.🛡️ **Licensing rules matter.** You will never be expected to knowingly break licensing rules to make staffing or scheduling easier.🏡 **A life outside of work matters, too.** **No weekends. 10 paid holidays PLUS 10 additional paid days off.** Predictable scheduling and real time away from work.❤️ **Work with a purpose.** Spend your days helping children become capable, confident, kind, and independent within a Catholic Montessori community where your work matters.**If you want to be treated like an educator, do meaningful work, be part of a professional team, and still have a life outside of your job—we invite you to join us.**

jobs.title: Strength and Conditioning Coach at Peak Performance Training - Maryville
jobs.description: Employer: Peak Performance Training - Maryville Expires: 11/19/2026 AboutPeak Performance Training Peak Performance Training is a coaching-first strength and conditioning facility in Maryville, TN, serving youth athletes and adults. Our tagline is Climb Higher - we believe capability can be built, consistency beats intensity, and coaching begins with understanding the person in front of you before prescribing anything. We're not chasing hype or quick fixes. We're building real relationships and real, evidence-based development, one session at a time. The RoleThis is a coaching-first position. Your job is to deliver high-quality, high-energy sessions that meet Peak's coaching standard, and to run a coaching process that drives real client development - for athletes and adults both. Peak believes coaches, not programs, are what actually change people's trajectories. This role exists because we believe that, and we're looking for someone who believes it too. We're not looking for someone who already knows our system - we'll teach you that. We're looking for someone who wants to give back through coaching, who's a student of the craft, and who we can trust to represent Peak on the floor. What You'll DoDeliver Peak's coaching standard every session: Explain–Cue–Demo, visual language, 1:1 feedback, full engagement with every athlete and client in the room Come prepared - know what, who, and how you're coaching each week, before the week starts Log PRs and milestones for your athletes and clients Keep equipment and facility standards tight Work through a structured onboarding: culture and coaching fundamentals first, then technical systems, then live reps with feedback, extending into adult coaching once trust is established Participate in a real review rhythm - weekly check-ins, weekly programming meetings, and quarterly performance reviews - not a "figure it out yourself" environment. What Success Looks LikeConsistent execution of Peak's coaching standard, tracked and reviewed, not just assumed At least one PR or milestone logged per client per month Reliable, proactive weekly preparation - not scrambling day-of Growing trust and responsibility over time, including eventual input into how Peak runs as a business Requirements CPR/AED certified CSCS or SCCC certification required Strength & conditioning coaching background preferred Reliable transportation; full availability for the role's session times, including early mornings, regardless of commute distanceCoachable, hungry to learn, and driven by a genuine desire to help people - not just to coachCompensation & Perks Salary: 38,000–40,000/year salaryCSCS exam/renewal supportFree Peak training/membershipTeam dinners, gear, and recognitionPaid time offRetirement and health insurance: not part of the initial offer, under consideration for the future How to Apply Send a resume and references to greg@peakperformancetrainingtn.com.

jobs.description: Employer: Event Partners Inc. (EPI) Expires: 11/19/2026 Be part of the action. Work the events you love. At EPI, you don't just work a job—you get to be part of the experience. Our event staff are on the front lines of professional and collegiate sporting events, concerts, festivals, and major events throughout the Charleston area. If you enjoy being around people, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want a job where no two events are exactly the same, EPI gives you the opportunity to experience live events from a completely different perspective. From the moment the gates open to the final whistle, encore, or closing announcement, you are part of making the event happen. What You'll Do: EPI provides event management and staffing for a wide variety of live events. Depending on the event, you may work in roles including: Parking and traffic operationsTicket taking and guest entrySecurity screeningUshers and guest servicesCrowd managementHospitality and suite servicesAccess controlBarricade operationsBack-of-house event operationsAnd much moreYou could spend one shift helping fans find their seats at a college football game, the next assisting with a concert, and another working behind the scenes at a major festival. Every event is different. Every shift is an opportunity to be part of something happening in your community. This is a PART-TIME, EVENT-BASED opportunity serving the Charleston, South Carolina area. Our schedules are built around live events, which means this is a great opportunity for individuals looking for flexible part-time work while still wanting to be involved in an exciting environment. Whether you're looking for additional income, enjoy sports and entertainment, want to meet new people, or simply want a job that's more interesting than sitting behind a desk, EPI puts you where the action is. You'll gain valuable experience in customer service, event operations, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving—all while working alongside a team responsible for helping some of the area's biggest events run successfully. Who We're Looking For We are looking for people who are: Reliable – If you accept a shift, we need you to show up and be ready to work.Outgoing – You're comfortable interacting with guests and working with a team.Energetic – Live events move quickly, and we need people who can keep up.Professional – You represent EPI and our clients every time you put on the uniform.Team-oriented – Great events happen when everyone works together.Customer-focused – You can remain friendly and professional, even when situations get challenging. RequirementsMust be 18 years of age or olderMust have a High School Diploma or GEDMust be able to pass a background checkMust maintain a neat and presentable appearanceMust be able to stand and remain active for extended periods of timeMust be able to provide excellent customer service in a variety of situationsMust be dependable and committed to working the shifts you accept Why EPI?Because work doesn't have to feel like work. At EPI, you can experience live sporting events, concerts, festivals, and other major events while playing an important role in making them successful. You're not sitting in the stands—you're behind the scenes, on the field level, at the gates, in the crowd, and in the middle of the action. If you're dependable, energetic, and ready to be part of something bigger than a typical part-time job, we want you on the EPI team.We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

jobs.description: Employer: Psypawlogy Pet Care LLC Expires: 11/19/2026 Psypawlogy Pet Care LLC · Serving clients throughout the DMV area (Washington, DC, Northern Virginia and Maryland)About PsypawlogyPsypawlogy is a psychology-informed pet care company founded by a doctor of psychology, currently serving clients all around the DMV area. We believe pets thrive when care is built around how they think, feel and learn, so we apply principles from behavioral science and psychology to every visit.That means we use positive reinforcement and low-stress handling, and we read each animal's body language to understand how they're feeling. We keep routines consistent so pets feel safe while their people are away, and we offer enrichment that engages their minds as well as their bodies. Specialists who join us gain hands-on experience applying these principles. That makes this a great fit for anyone studying psychology, animal behavior, veterinary science or a related field.About this opportunityThis is an independent contractor opportunity, not employment. In your letter, tell us which services you'd like to offer, your general availability, the parts of the DMV area you can serve, and what draws you to working with animals.

jobs.description: Employer: STRIDE Academy Expires: 11/19/2026 STRIDE Academy in St. Cloud, MN, stands out as a K-8 public charter school with a strong focus on the whole child, celebrated for fostering academic excellence and a nurturing learning environment. Our mission emphasizes individualized learning and innovative teaching, preparing students for future success. Notable for our community involvement and award-winning programs, STRIDE offers a unique, supportive educational experience that cultivates curiosity and character development, making a significant impact on our students and the wider community. POSITION DETAILSTitle: Special Education Behavior Intervention TeacherGrade: 8Start Date: 2026-2027Full Time FTE: 1.0 POSITION OVERVIEWThe Eighth Grade Special Education Teacher provides individualized academic instruction and targeted behavior intervention for eighth-grade students with disabilities at STRIDE Academy. This position combines the instructional and case management responsibilities of a special education teacher with a focus on helping students strengthen self-regulation, engagement, and the skills needed to access learning and make academic progress.The teacher develops and implements Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), delivers specially designed instruction, and uses academic and behavioral data to guide student supports. Working with general education teachers, paraprofessionals, related service providers, administration, and families, the teacher creates a safe, structured, and inclusive learning environment and supports students as they prepare for high school. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIESAcademic Instruction and Student ProgressPlan and deliver specially designed instruction in reading, writing, mathematics, and other identified areas based on student needs and IEP goals.Develop lesson plans, instructional materials, and assessments that support access to eighth-grade curriculum and address individual skill gaps.Provide individual, small-group, and classroom-based instruction as determined by student IEPs and service needs.Implement accommodations, modifications, assistive technology, and other supports to increase student participation and independence.Collect and analyze assessment results, work samples, and progress monitoring data; adjust instruction and interventions to improve student outcomes.Teach organization, task initiation, work completion, study skills, self-advocacy, and other executive functioning skills that support academic success.Behavior Assessment and InterventionConduct functional behavioral assessments (FBAs) as part of the evaluation and IEP team process; collect and analyze data to identify behavior patterns, contributing factors, and student support needs.Develop, implement, monitor, and revise Positive Behavior Support Plans (PBSPs) or Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) with the IEP team and align supports with student IEPs.Provide explicit instruction in self-regulation, coping strategies, social skills, problem-solving, and replacement behaviors that support participation in learning.Establish predictable routines, clear expectations, positive reinforcement, and individualized supports that promote safety, responsibility, and engagement.Use approved prevention and de-escalation strategies, respond to behavioral crises within training and school procedures, and support students in returning to instruction.Document behavioral incidents and intervention outcomes; collaborate with administration and the special education team regarding disciplinary removals, readmission supports, and required procedures or reporting.Use restrictive procedures only when authorized, trained, and permitted by applicable law and school procedures; complete required documentation and participate in follow-up reviews.IEP Case Management and ComplianceServe as the special education case manager for assigned students and coordinate IEP development, implementation, annual reviews, and progress reporting.Coordinate and participate in evaluations and reevaluations; facilitate IEP and Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) meetings and complete required special education documentation.Maintain accurate, timely records of services, academic and behavioral progress, parent communication, assessments, and due process documentation.Coordinate service schedules and communicate student accommodations, modifications, and behavior supports to staff responsible for implementation.Work with the IEP team to ensure services and documentation meet applicable federal and Minnesota special education requirements and school procedures.Collaborate with families, receiving high school staff, and the IEP team to support the transition to ninth grade, including sharing relevant instructional and behavior supports and completing transition planning as applicable.Collaboration and Student SupportPartner with eighth-grade teachers to align instruction, coordinate assignments and assessments, and support student access to general education settings.Guide assigned paraprofessionals in implementing instructional plans, accommodations, and behavior supports; provide modeling, feedback, and clear daily expectations.Communicate regularly and professionally with parents and guardians about student strengths, needs, progress, and strategies for support.Collaborate with related service providers, school leadership, and Child Study or CARE Teams as assigned to address academic, behavioral, social-emotional, and attendance concerns.Build positive student relationships and support routines across classrooms, hallways, lunch, arrival, dismissal, and transportation settings as relevant to assigned students.Reinforce schoolwide expectations and use restorative problem-solving approaches consistent with student plans and school practices.Professional ResponsibilitiesParticipate in professional development, professional learning communities, staff meetings, and assigned student support teams.Maintain required crisis prevention and intervention training, such as CPI or Ukeru, as applicable to the assignment; provide staff training only when qualified and authorized.Protect student confidentiality, maintain professional boundaries, and meet schedules, deadlines, and professional responsibilities.Perform other related duties as assigned.REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONSBachelor’s degree required; Preferably in Special Education, Social Work, Psychology or related fieldValid Minnesota teaching license in special education appropriate to the assigned grade level and students served, or eligibility to obtain the required license before beginning the assignment.Three or more years of experience working with students with behavioral and social-emotional needs in school settings.Knowledge of specially designed instruction, differentiated teaching, assessment, IEP development, due process requirements, and progress monitoring.Demonstrated knowledge of FBAs, individualized behavior plans, positive behavior supports, and crisis prevention and de-escalation strategies.Ability to deliver academic instruction while supporting students with significant behavioral and social-emotional needs.Preferred QualificationsExperience teaching middle school students, managing a special education caseload, and supporting students with emotional or behavioral disabilities.Training in trauma-informed practices, restorative approaches, and approved crisis prevention and intervention methods.Skills & CompetenciesStrong instructional planning, classroom management, organization, and documentation skills.Ability to analyze academic and behavioral data and adjust instruction and supports accordingly.Clear, respectful communication and effective collaboration with students, staff, and families.Ability to remain calm, consistent, and supportive during challenging situations.Proficiency with educational technology and student data systems.Commitment to individualized learning, equitable practices, and the academic and personal growth of every student. BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION Salary Range: Starting salary of $60,000 or higher based on experience per contract yearBenefits: Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, retirement, and professional development opportunities APPLICATION PROCESSApplication Materials: Submit a resume, cover letter, references, and complete online application Application Deadline: Until FilledContact Information: Niki Krier, Special Education Director, nkrier@strideacademy.orgApply here: https://www.strideacademy.org/employment EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT STRIDE Academy is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. CALL TO ACTION Join our dedicated team at STRIDE Academy and make a difference in the lives of our students. Apply today to contribute to our vibrant learning community where every child is encouraged to reach their full potential. We look forward to welcoming you to our team!

jobs.description: Employer: Partners In Excellence Expires: 11/19/2026 Are you passionate about making an impact on the life of a child and helping them reach their greatest potential?Join us as a Behavior Therapist and be a part of an amazing team, dedicated to improving the lives of children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through providing early intensive therapies to young children. Partners offers both full-time and part-time positions, working Monday-Friday between the hours of 8:00am-5:00pm.Partners In Excellence (Partners) is a premier autism therapy center providing autism therapy services to children in a healthcare setting.Our autism therapy center provides simulated environments that reflect real-life situations, enabling the children to work on their skills one-on-one or in small groups with trained behavior therapists.Through our paid two-week premiere training program, you will be equipped with the skills needed to apply ABA techniques to implement targeted curriculum with a variety of teaching techniques.Clinical staff will provide you with supervision, ongoing coaching, and professional development opportunities as you accumulate your clinical/supervision hours.All new staff are assigned a mentor upon hireThe salary range for this position is: $20 - $33.12 per hour. This range reflects the base salary for this position. Please note that the specific compensation for this role will be determined based on your experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.Benefits of Working at Partners:Competitive payMedical, Dental, and Vision InsuranceShort and Long-Term Disability401(k) retirement savings plan with employer matchEmployee Assistance ProgramCasual Dress EnvironmentPaid HolidaysPaid Time OffFlexible Spending AccountsLife InsuranceEmployee Appreciation EventsKudos Recognition ProgramEmployee Referral Bonus ProgramCollaborative, empathetic, supportive, and rewarding company cultureResponsibilitiesWorks under supervision to provide direct therapy to a team of 4-6 clients following client treatment plans ensuring goals and objectives are being metDocuments therapy services accurately and timely (e.g., daily treatment notes, data collection, reporting parent and Partners In Excellence communications and client information)Ability to read written treatment directions, collect numeric data, and write progress notesIn order to effectively fulfill the duties of a BT, you will have access to protected health information (PHI) of many of Partners’ Clients. It is your responsibility to be fully knowledgeable of Partners in Excellence’s Privacy Policies and Procedures and to report any violations to their direct and/or clinical supervisor (see Partners’ Policies and Procedures – HIPAA). It is the responsibility of the BT to protect Partners’ Clients’ privacy at and away from workCompletes the required technical training and participates in ongoing training opportunitiesRedirects, intervenes, observes, and monitors client behaviorsAbility to problem solve and make appropriate decisionPossesses the interpersonal skills to be playful, enthusiastic, and bring a high level of energy into the therapeutic situationAbility to work with a team and accept corrective feedback, complying with supervisory directionEffective communication skills with parents, co-workers, and supervisorsMakes sound decisions and uses good judgment when dealing with clients, parents, and co-workersDemonstrates dependability and consistency in therapy and other job-related activitiesCommunicates daily progress and client concerns to the appropriate staff membersOrganizes and cleans clients’ space and equipmentAssists in keeping the facility safe, organized, sanitary, and guides others to do the sameAssists clients with personal care including dressing, toileting, personal hygiene, food, nutrition, and diet needsAbility to lift fifty (50) poundsAttends and participates in meetingsReports all safety concerns to the Center Manager or their direct supervisorThe BT is assigned to an area or areas (i.e., POD) at the Partners in Excellence’s center-based programsOther duties as assigned Physical Demands The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to communicate and interact with other members of the organization and parent/guardians of the clients. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus. Additional physical demands: Lift/carry/hold up to 25-50 pounds Push/pull up to 25-50 pounds Shoulder movement such as reach above, wipe tables, sweep/mop Use OSHA approved step stool/ladder as needed Walk, run, squat, bend, twist, kneel, crouch, crawl Ability move quickly with assigned client Finger and hand grasping/squeezing Qualifications We require candidates to have:High School diplomaMust be at least 18 years of ageSuccessfully passed an initial and subsequent background checks (no history of felonies, substantiated client maltreatment or vulnerable adult incidents, or disqualifying misdemeanors)We prefer candidates to have:Previous behavioral therapy experienceBachelor’s degree in related fieldKnowledge of teaching procedures associated with Verbal Behavior TherapyGeneral knowledge of typical and special needs clientsPartners offers both full-time and part-time positions, working Monday-Friday between the hours of 8:00am-5:00pm.To learn more about starting a rewarding career with an innovative, exciting company that offers room for promotion and advancement, please visit our website at www.partnersmn.com.Individuals with experience working with culturally diverse populations are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Special Education Support Specialist at Rochester Beacon Academy
jobs.description: Employer: Rochester Beacon Academy Expires: 11/19/2026 SPECIAL EDUCATION SUPPORT SPECIALISTRochester Beacon Academy is seeking a Special Education Support Specialist for the 2026-2027 school year. Rochester Beacon Academy (RBA) is a 6th-12th grade charter school that places a strong emphasis on providing individualized attention to students. The school has small class sizes, allowing teachers to provide students with focused and personalized instruction. RBA also has a special focus on serving students with special education needs, with close to 80% of the student body receiving such services. The administration and staff are dedicated to providing these students with the support and resources they need to succeed in school and beyond. RBA has a caring and compassionate culture, with teachers and staff committed to creating a safe, joyful and inclusive learning environment. The administration places a high value on work-life balance for both students and staff, recognizing the importance of a healthy work-life balance for academic success. In addition, the school uses trauma-informed practices to support and respect students in ways that acknowledge and address the impact of past traumatic experiences. These practices help create a safe and supportive learning environment that promotes emotional healing and academic success. Overall, the charter school is a small, caring educational institution that is committed to providing a supportive and inclusive learning environment for students, particularly those with special education needs.Your job responsibilities includes but are not limited to:Schedule IEPs and evaluation meetings.Upload IEPs and related information into SPED forms.Organize daily transportation routes, communication, etc.Maintain staff calling trees and voicemails through Marco.Transfer SPED records to all appropriate agencies (Bluestem, Prairie Care, etc).Assign subs for licensed and non-licensed staff daily due to PTO schedule.Maintain all SPED paper files in a concise and accurate manner that meets compliance with the State of MN.Support program staff.Be available to answer to stakeholders on inclement weather days (WILD Days).Knowledgeable of all office equipment.Knowledgeable about all district policy.Assists with organizing of records, maintaining of Special Education student folders, and other permanent records assigned and while protecting confidentiality of student records and information. Schedules students for testing and assessment appointments. Provides support in Special Education enrollment and identification.Participate in department and program training and meetings.Facilitates successful monitoring and completion of compliance checklists of IEPs as meetings occur.This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive, and employees will also perform other reasonable related business duties as assigned by their immediate supervisor and other management.Minimum Qualifications: High School Diploma or equivalent Clerical/Office experience Knowledge of Microsoft Office Programs Knowledge of SPED FormsKnowledge of Special Education timelines in compliance with MDE.Ability to organize tasks and complete within desired deadline Attention to detailPay: $36,000.00 - $55,000.00 per year based on experience and qualificationsBenefits:Dental insuranceHealth insuranceHealth savings accountLife insurancePaid time offRetirement planVision insuranceSchedule and Location:Full TimeMonday to Friday In PersonRochester, MN 55902: Relocate before starting work (Required)If interested in applying, please complete the following:1. Copy of Teaching License if present4. 2 Letters of Recommendation or ReferencesCompleted materials can be emailed to our Executive Director at beth.bruns@rochesterbeaconacademy.org
