jobs.description: Employer: LEAD Public Schools Expires: 11/19/2026 JOB TITLE: Special Education Teacher (Exceptional Education)REPORTS TO: Principal Be a LEADer: Teach Exceptional Education at LEAD Public SchoolsSpecial Education (Ex.Ed) teachers are champions for equality within the school, ensuring that students’ needs are met. Our ideal Special Education teacher is passionate about supporting students with IEPs, advocating for those who need the most support, and continually growing as an educator. Flexibility, coachability, and a commitment to excellence are key qualities for this role. The LEAD EnvironmentEx.Ed teachers at LEAD work relentlessly with their teammates to:Enhance students’ reading abilities, enabling them to explore historical events and gain a broader understanding of the world.Help students meet Tennessee standards by the end of the year.This work is supported through:Coaching and support from administration.Regular feedback and collaboration with colleagues.Data analysis and targeted instruction to help students overcome challenges and rise above grade-level expectations. What We Are Looking ForSuccessful teachers at LEAD:Put in extra effort to ensure students have access to a high-quality education.Persevere through challenges, set ambitious goals, and never give up on students.Are flexible, hard-working, and committed to improving their classroom abilities to meet students’ needs.We are seeking Exceptional Education teachers who embody these qualities. Position ResponsibilitiesPrimary ResponsibilitiesDesign and implement data-driven lesson plans to support students with cognitive and/or developmental delays.Develop individualized education programs (IEPs) for students.Maintain special education files (both paper and electronic) in compliance with federal, state, and local guidelines.Collect data on individual student skills to measure progress toward IEP goals and assess program effectiveness.Provide functional curriculum and focus on daily living skills, as appropriate.Foster independence in students across all natural settings.Advocate for and facilitate students’ exposure to general education peers and settings, as appropriate.Plan and implement instructional and/or behavioral strategies to ensure all students can access academic content.Other ResponsibilitiesDirect and supervise education assistants to provide effective classroom programs and address individual student needs.Support general classroom teachers in implementing established curricula and individual student plans. QualificationsExperience:Minimum of two years teaching experience preferred but not required.Prior experience with diverse student populations or in an urban setting preferred.Education/Certification:Bachelor’s degree required.Must hold:(a) A valid Tennessee teaching license with the appropriate endorsement to teach SPED, OR(b) A valid out-of-state license transferable to Tennessee within 90 days of employment, OR(c) Proof of progress toward Tennessee certification.Physical Demands:Light to medium physical work involving standing, walking, lifting, pushing, and carrying (exerting up to 20 pounds).Other Qualifications or Characteristics:Belief in LEAD’s mission that all students are capable of success while preparing them for college and life.Evidence of self-motivation and willingness to be a team player.COMPENSATION AND BENEFITSLEAD Public Schools offers an innovative performance-based compensation plan for teachers. This plan allows us to transparently reward our teachers not by how many years they have worked but rather by their positive impact on students and schools, evidenced by their consistent performance in and out of the classroom. Teachers receive a competitive base salary with the potential for a signing bonus and can earn up to 10% on their base salary each year through our performance-based compensation plan. This plan has been in place for 5 years, and we have seen an average annual increase of over 5% for our teachers with approximately 80% retention for those who qualify. Additionally, teachers are eligible for LEAD’s Master Teacher program after 3 years. In this program, teachers can earn up to $100,000 and receive a $1,500 professional development stipend. Robust and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, disability, supplemental insurance, life insurance policy options, and mental health benefits. Application for these benefits may be made immediately upon employment. The policy is effective upon the first of the month following the first day of work.Certificated staff have access to the Tennessee Consolidated Retirement System pension plan (TCRS). Eligible staff contribute 5%, and LEAD matches up to 6%. Staff may also be eligible for 401k, in which LEAD will contribute 5%. Participation in TCRS is mandated by the state of TN. Non-TCRS eligible staff members are eligible to participate in LEAD’s defined contribution 403b plan. LEAD matches 50% of the first 6% of employee contributions. Additional annual contributions are provided to eligible employees after one year based on LEAD’s overall budget performance. Participation in this plan is voluntary.The time off package for school-year employees (teachers, counselors, paraprofessionals) includes 30 paid days during the school year (including holidays, fall break, thanksgiving break, winter break, and spring break). School-year employees also receive summer break. In addition to breaks and holidays, school-year employees can accrue up to 10 PTO days during the school year. The time off package for calendar-year employees (Central office, Instructional Managers, Assistant Principals) includes 32 paid days during the school year (including holidays, fall break, thanksgiving break, winter break, spring break). In addition to breaks and holidays, school-year employees can accrue up to 12 PTO days during the school year. Parental leave - 16 weeks of paid maternity leave and 6 weeks of paid parental leave (adoption, foster care). Teachers are provided with laptop computers with access to the internet and or email to assist them in performing their job responsibilities. jobs.description: Employer: United Community Center Expires: 11/19/2026 UCC On- Call Substitute Teachers provide high-quality instruction and classroom management across UCC schools during short- and long-term staff absences. They maintain instructional continuity, uphold a positive learning environment, and foster academic and social-emotional growth in accordance with UCC policies. In long-term assignments, substitutes assume full teacher responsibilities. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:Core Duties & ResponsibilitiesInstruction & Curriculum: Deliver standards-based, differentiated lesson plans; adapt instruction for diverse learners (including EL and IEP students); and utilize effective questioning, technology, and formative assessments to drive student achievement.Classroom Management & SEL: Maintain a safe, structured, and culturally responsive environment; apply proactive, positive behavior support; integrate Tier 1 SEL practices; and supervise students across all school settings (classroom, cafeteria, playground).Communication & Collaboration: Maintain open communication with families, administrators, and staff; participate in parent conferences; collaborate with support teams (MTSS, 504, IEP, counselors); and leave detailed handover notes for returning teachers.Professionalism & Operations: Adapt flexibly to daily coverage assignments across buildings and subjects; follow all district policies and safety protocols; adhere to administrative expectations (punctuality, confidentiality, accurate bi-weekly timesheets); and engage in staff meetings and professional growth.Qualifications & Key SkillsKnowledge & Pedagogy: Strong understanding of K–8 content, pedagogical strategies, classroom management, and routines.Adaptability & Multitasking: Ability to pivot quickly across grade levels, environments, and subject areas while solving problems effectively under changing needs.Interpersonal & Communication Skills: Excellent oral and written communication skills to engage effectively with students, parents, and diverse staff.Technical & Administrative Proficiency: Basic computer skills (Google Workspace, Word, Excel, email) and strong organizational/time-management abilities.Professional Attributes: Dependable, reflective, culturally responsive, and dedicated to student growth and continuous learning.Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned by their supervisor to support students, colleagues, or the school community.QualificationsAssociate’s or Bachelor’s Degree required, as well as current Wisconsin DPI substitute teacher (or teacher) licensure required. Must possess strong oral and written communication skills. The candidate should be able to work independently with little direct supervision, work as part of a team, accept responsibilities, and be self-motivated. Must display effective multitasking and time management skills.Must have reliable transportation and be able to travel independently between buildings. jobs.title: (#R6663) Special Education Teacher (2026-2027 School Year)[Immediate Start]-$2,500 Signing Bonus! at DSST Public Schools (Denver, Colorado)
jobs.description: Employer: DSST Public Schools (Denver, Colorado) Expires: 11/19/2026 POSITION: Special Education Teacher (Mild/Moderate Setting)GRADE LEVEL: Hiring for both middle school and high school positionsLOCATION: Hiring at multiple locations. You can view the current openings at this link. We encourage you to apply even if your preferred position is not listed as we will be posting new roles throughout the year.SALARY: $62,000-$80,000 based on years of aligned experience up to 10 years and a $2,500 signing bonus for those with a Colorado Special Education endorsement. We also offer a relocation stipend for anyone joining us from 75 miles or more from Denver! STATUS: Full time school year, benefits eligible, exempt, in-person positionSTART: First day of new SpEd Teacher staff training will be at the end of July. You can view the current School Year Calendar here. THE ROLEOur Mild/Moderate Special Education Teachers are leaders who play an integral role in ensuring that students with disabilities are welcomed, known, and challenged to achieve their most ambitious post-secondary path. Learn more about a Day in the Life of a Special Education Teacher and why you should choose to grow your career at DSST here.Key Responsibilities:Be an IEP Case Manager: Serve as case manager to a portfolio of students; completing tasks such as writing data driven IEPs, developing goals, monitoring progress, delivering targeted academic & behavioral interventions, and celebrating success with each student’s team of teachers and family along the way. Ensure Students Receive Accommodations/Modifications: Partner with general education teachers to appropriately implement accommodations and modifications with intentionality and consistency. Advocate for and champion all diverse learners in the school by participating on the MTSS (Multi-Tiered Systems of Support) Team.Manage a Support Team: Based on a student’s services in their IEP, you may also supervise and develop paraprofessionals that serve as 1:1 support for that student. Deliver Rigorous & Engaging Content: In partnership with your general education teaching partner(s), utilize DSST’s curriculum resources to plan, intellectually prepare, and teach rigorous, culturally responsive, and grade level aligned content in co-taught/push-in settings. Track and Support Student Growth: Prioritize students’ intellectual growth by holding high expectations for academic success including monitoring and assessing the performance of all students through a variety of assessment tools and resources to guide instruction and support individual student proficiency.Promote Positive Culture: Employ DSST culture and support systems while validating students’ cultural identities. Actively promote a unified and positive classroom and school culture. Cultivate and maintain trusting relationships with students and families. Pursue Professional Development: Engage in professional growth opportunities, including regular coaching, feedback, and development, with a focus on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.Contribute to School Community: Undertake additional duties as needed, such as supporting student recruitment, after school tutoring, etc. Explore more potential duties here.THE PERSONWe value staff with diverse backgrounds, talents, and ideas. Our most successful employees share the following characteristics: An unwavering belief that all students can succeed in school and reach their most ambitious post-secondary goals.A proactive approach to learning and growth, welcoming feedback to enhance your teaching practice.Qualifications:If you are passionate about working with students with disabilities and you don’t currently have a teaching credential or have a teaching credential and would like to obtain your SpEd endorsement, we’d love to connect with you! Please email humancapital@scienceandtech.org. Minimum: Has both a teaching license and a special education endorsement. You can read more about obtaining a Colorado Special Education Endorsement here. We recommend reaching out to CDE directly for information on transferring your out of state credentials.Ideal: Proven commitment to and experience with serving students of color, students with disabilities, and/or multilingual students. Experience in teaching and implementing positive behavior supports to facilitate learning in the areas of academic, communication, executive functioning, behavioral, and social-emotional regulation.Please note: The DSST Talent Team replies to every application. If you haven’t heard from us by the indicated timeline, please check your spam folder first. If you don’t see an email there, reach out to us at humancapital@scienceandtech.org. We’re committed to providing an exceptional candidate experience.Application TimelineThis is an evergreen position, meaning DSST Public Schools recruits for this role on an ongoing basis to support current and anticipated hiring needs across our network. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and qualified candidates may be contacted for interviews as opportunities become available.For positions with a defined hiring timeline, the anticipated application deadline will be listed at the top of the job posting.Who We AreAt DSST Public Schools, we are proud to achieve transformational results for our 7,500+ students — 97% of whom attend a Green (top-rated) school. Just as important is how we achieve them: values-centered, human-focused, and together.We invite educators and leaders who share our belief that there is more in us — more brilliance, more courage, more possibility — to join us.Our Impact100% of DSST graduates have been admitted to college or a postsecondary program15 of 16 schools rated Green on the 2024–25 SPF9 out of 10 DSST families would recommend DSST to a friend95%+ of staff say their managers check in regularly and care about them as people Why Work at DSST?At DSST, our Quantum 5 Culture defines how we help every team member grow, belong, and thrive.Comprehensive Compensation & Benefits: Competitive pay and a Total Rewards package that includes fertility and adoption support, educator-focused mental-health care, and everyday perks like Safeway grocery discounts.Growth & Opportunity: Weekly 1:1 coaching, data-driven feedback, and clear career pathways such as Apprentice Teacher and Emerging Leader.Rewards & Recognition: Core Value and TOAST Awards, milestone celebrations, and the signature Flower Person Award honoring staff who help our community flourish.Whole Human Wellness: Access to the Therapist of Color Collaborative, Wellness Wednesdays, comprehensive health coverage, and six weeks of paid parental leave.Thriving in Colorado: Time to recharge with 11+ weeks off each year, relocation support for out of state applicants, and local discounts that help you enjoy life in our beautiful sunshine filled state.Learn more about our Quantum 5 Culture and Compensation & Benefits.Employment Classification & PERA ParticipationDSST Public Schools participates in the Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association (PERA). Unless otherwise stated in the position title or posting, all roles are full-time and are designated as PERA-covered positions. Candidates should review their individual circumstances and ensure they are able to accept employment in a PERA-covered role prior to applying.EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY AND DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSIONDSST Public Schools is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not exclude participation in, deny benefits to, or discriminate against any person on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex (including pregnancy and related conditions, sexual orientation, or gender identity), age (40 and older), disability, or genetic information. We also prohibit retaliation for filing a complaint, reasonably opposing discrimination, or participating in any investigation or proceeding.DSST is committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace where all individuals are respected, valued, and empowered to thrive.PHYSICAL DEMANDSThe physical demands described here represent those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing these duties, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear and may spend extended periods standing, walking, bending, or kneeling. The employee must occasionally lift or move up to 30 pounds and have sufficient hand and finger dexterity to operate a computer keyboard and other office equipment.

jobs.title: Behavior Technician at Ad Astra Behavior Analytic Services
jobs.description: Employer: Ad Astra Behavior Analytic Services Expires: 11/19/2026 This position provides a strong entry point or advancement opportunity for individuals interested in building a career in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA). As a Behavior Technician, you will carry out personalized ABA treatment plans and provide direct support to children and their families in home-based and community settings, based on each client's needs. Typical work hours are Monday through Friday between 3:00 PM and 8:00 PM, with scheduling flexibility available. Hourly pay ranges from $20 to $27 and is based on relevant experience and credentials. Applicants who are fluent in Spanish may qualify for increased compensation.Position SummaryBehavior Technicians work directly with children in individualized, one-on-one sessions to develop essential skills such as communication, social engagement, and daily living abilities. The role involves applying research-supported ABA interventions to decrease challenging behaviors while encouraging independence, safety, and positive growth. Candidates who thrive in this role often have experience working with children, exposure to ABA or related helping professions, or academic backgrounds in psychology, education, social work, or similar fields. Dependability, patience, and a genuine passion for helping others are critical for success.QualificationsApplicants must possess a high school diploma or GED, hold a valid driver's license, and have dependable transportation with active auto insurance that lists the technician as a covered driver. All candidates are required to successfully complete a Live Scan background check and provide proof of a negative TB test. Strong professionalism, problem-solving skills, creativity, and effective communication are essential, along with the ability to work collaboratively within a team environment. The position also involves physical activity, including lifting up to 50 pounds.We offer competitive wages, adaptable scheduling, and a welcoming, supportive work culture focused on professional development and growth. All newly hired employees are required to complete a company-sponsored 40-hour online Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training program before beginning client services.Other benefits include:Paid Time Off (PTO), sick leave, mileage reimbursement, and drive time payComplimentary 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training and professional development opportunitiesStructured performance-based pay increases, including raises for consistent availability and RBT certification Incentive Pay Structure$1/hour raise after maintaining consistent availability for 90 consecutive daysAdditional $1/hour raise upon successfully earning RBT certificationAdditional $1/hour raise for completing the 40 hours of RBT training Cancellation PolicyTo protect staff time and earnings, we maintain a clear cancellation policy. Paid cancellations are provided for up to 2 hours of pay if a client cancels within 30 minutes or less of the scheduled start time and/or technician has already departed for the session. We also actively monitor and address excessive client cancellations to protect technician schedules and maintain consistent hours. Our CommitmentWe are dedicated to the success of every Behavior Technician, offering paid initial training and ongoing learning opportunities. At Ad Astra, our mission is to foster a culture of guided independence, delivering an engaging client experience that builds meaningful skills and long-term outcomes for today, tomorrow, and beyond.Ad Astra Behavior Analytic Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer, considering all qualified applicants in accordance with federal, state, and local laws. Qualifications for this role include strong communication skills, teamwork ability, experience with the pediatric population.

jobs.title: Preschool Teacher at Bambinis Playschool
jobs.description: Employer: Bambinis Playschool Expires: 11/19/2026 Looking for the next member of our preschool family. We love being active and outdoors! Biking, hiking, playing in creeks, climbing trees, sledding, ice skating, skiing, soccer, gymnastics, and swim! We love bugs, playing in our mud kitchen and tending to our garden! We love the earth and always work hard to show love and kindness to every living thing. In our classroom, we are immersed in magic. Intentional in-depth units of inquiry, beautiful and engaging materials and teachers who truly love to teach. We learn through play and would love for you to come play too!We are a small nature based, Reggio inspired program, located at the base of Pattee Canyon. Ages range from 2-5. Families are very close, involved and supportive. Very loving environment to be a part of! We are looking for someone who is patient with a loving and compassionate heart. Who possesses qualities of maturity and a desire and willingness to learn. We need a teammate who has a strong work ethic, is punctual and dependable and truly enjoys the simple things in life. We love to laugh and have a lot of fun spending time with these beautiful little humans. Our program runs from Sept-May (M-TH 8-4), but there is opportunity to provide private summer care for enrolled families if interested. The open position is flexible for the time being, but will need to be full time as of Fall 2027. This is when our current co-lead will be moving away! The hours would then be 7:30am-5pm M-TH.Position is hourly and DOE (Perks are offered after probationary period). A background check, CPR and trainings are required by the state, which we can take care of once hired.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: SAT Tutor Trainer at Kyo Standard Test Prep
jobs.description: Employer: Kyo Standard Test Prep Expires: 11/19/2026 SAT Tutor Trainer / Test Prep Training SpecialistWho We’re Looking ForWe’re looking for a true test-prep professional—and you know who you are.You have extensive experience working with students across the full scoring range, from students who need to master foundational skills to high achievers pursuing scores of 1500 and above. More importantly, you have a proven track record of producing meaningful, measurable score improvements.You understand that excellent test preparation requires more than content knowledge. It requires accurately diagnosing why a student is struggling, selecting the right strategy, explaining concepts clearly, building confidence, and holding students accountable.Now, we’re looking for someone who can pass that expertise on to our tutors.This position will begin part-time, with the potential to transition into a full-time role as our training needs and tutoring team continue to grow.About the RoleKyo Standard Test Prep is seeking an experienced SAT educator to train, coach, and develop our growing team of tutors.This is not primarily a student-tutoring position. Your main responsibility will be helping our tutors consistently deliver high-quality instruction using Kyo Standard’s curriculum, strategies, and teaching methods.You will lead new-tutor training, conduct teach-backs and role-plays, observe lessons, evaluate tutor performance, and provide direct, actionable feedback. You will also help us strengthen our curriculum, training materials, and academic standards as the company grows.The ideal candidate combines deep SAT expertise with the ability to develop other educators. You should be comfortable leading group training, identifying instructional weaknesses, giving honest and constructive feedback, and holding tutors accountable to high standards.ResponsibilitiesTrain newly hired tutors in Kyo Standard’s SAT curriculum, instructional strategies, and student-management expectations.Lead live online training sessions, workshops, role-plays, and tutor teach-backs.Conduct occasional in-person training sessions when needed.Ensure tutors can accurately and effectively teach SAT Math and SAT Reading and Writing.Train tutors to diagnose student weaknesses, develop appropriate study plans, and adjust instruction based on student performance.Teach tutors how to work with students across the full scoring range, from those scoring below 1000 to those pursuing scores of 1500 or higher.Coach tutors on test-taking strategies, time management, question analysis, elimination methods, and efficient problem-solving.Observe live lessons and review recorded sessions to evaluate instructional accuracy, organization, engagement, and adherence to Kyo Standard’s methods.Provide tutors with specific, actionable feedback and individualized improvement plans.Evaluate whether newly trained tutors are ready to work independently with students.Identify tutors who need additional training, coaching, or content support.Lead ongoing professional-development sessions covering student motivation, homework compliance, score plateaus, test anxiety, parent communication, and working with high-achieving students.Collaborate with leadership and curriculum developers to improve lesson plans, assessments, question banks, instructional resources, and training materials.Identify recurring challenges across the tutoring team and develop targeted training to address them.Maintain accurate records of training completion, tutor evaluations, coaching notes, and performance.Help establish and maintain consistent instructional standards across the entire tutoring team.What Success Looks LikeA successful SAT Tutor Trainer develops tutors who can:Teach SAT concepts and strategies accurately and consistently.Diagnose why a student is missing questions instead of simply reviewing the correct answers.Adapt their instruction to different score levels, learning needs, and student goals.Deliver engaging, organized, and student-centered lessons.Explain complex concepts in clear, accessible language.Set expectations and hold students accountable for completing their work.Respond effectively when students are unmotivated, overwhelmed, or falling behind.Help students overcome score plateaus and achieve measurable improvement.Communicate professionally with students, parents, and the Kyo Standard team.Consistently deliver the quality of instruction Kyo Standard families expect.Required QualificationsExtensive experience teaching or tutoring students for the SAT.A demonstrated record of helping students achieve meaningful score improvements.Experience working with students across a wide range of starting scores and academic abilities.Expert-level knowledge of the Digital SAT’s structure, timing, content, question types, and scoring.Strong knowledge of SAT Math, SAT Reading and Writing, or both.A deep understanding of test-taking strategy—not simply subject-matter knowledge.The ability to explain complex ideas clearly and model excellent instruction.Strong diagnostic skills and the ability to identify why a student or tutor is struggling.Experience training, mentoring, managing, or coaching tutors, teachers, or other educators.Confidence leading group training, workshops, and professional-development sessions.The ability to provide direct, constructive feedback while maintaining positive professional relationships.Excellent written and verbal communication skills.Strong organizational skills, reliability, and attention to detail.Comfort using online teaching platforms, video conferencing software, and digital educational tools.Preferred QualificationsExperience developing SAT curriculum, practice questions, lesson plans, or training materials.Experience training or managing a remote team of tutors.Experience reviewing recorded lessons and providing performance coaching.Familiarity with ACT preparation in addition to the SAT.Classroom teaching, instructional coaching, academic leadership, or department-management experience.Experience working with students who receive testing accommodations.Experience helping high-performing students pursue scores of 1500 or higher.About Kyo StandardKyo Standard Test Prep helps students achieve significant score improvements through expert instruction, structured practice, individualized support, and consistent accountability.Our students enter our programs with a wide range of starting scores and goals. Some need to strengthen foundational academic skills, while others are competing for admission to the country’s most selective colleges and universities.We believe the quality of a test-prep program ultimately depends on the quality of its tutors. We are looking for an experienced test-prep professional who can help us build an exceptional, consistent, and results-driven instructional team.How to ApplyIf you are an accomplished test-prep educator who enjoys developing other teachers, improving instructional quality, and building high-performing academic teams, we would love to hear from you.Please submit your résumé and a brief description of:Your SAT or ACT teaching experience.The range of student scores and ability levels you have worked with.Examples of score improvements your students have achieved.Your experience training, coaching, or managing other educators.
